1.

Applicant has filed this bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 for grant of regular bail as he has been arrested in connection with Crime No.0045/2024,
registered at Police Station - Telibandha, Raipur District - Raipur (C.G.) for offence punishable under Section 420 and 120- B of the Indian Penal Code.
2.

Learned counsel for objector raises an objection with regard to Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:9496 maintainability of this bail application on the ground that applicant has made prayer before the Hon'ble Supreme Court for his release on bail vide I.A. No.46618 filed in Special Leave Petition (Criminal) No. 462 of 2024.

sentences.text: Learned Senior counsel appearing on behalf of applicant replying to the objection submits that the objection is not sustainable because the contents of the I.A. No. 46618 would show that reasons assigned for filing of interlocutory application is that police registered the instant crime only to frustrate the order passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court dated 10.01.2024 in S.L.P. (Crl.) No. 462 of 2024 granting interim protection in a proceedings filed against rejection of anticipatory bail application by this Court.

He contended that police arrested the applicant on 14.02.2024 without complying with the directions of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar & Anr. , reported in (2014) 8 SCC 273 and in case of Md. Asfak Alam Vs. State of Jharkhand & Anr.,
reported in (2023) 8 SCC 632.

sentences.text: In interlocutory application, it is mentioned that applicant preferred a bail application when he was produced before the learned jurisdictional Magistrate in remand, which was dismissed on 15.02.2024.
In the prayer clause of that application, applicant has mentioned that applicant has been illegally and unlawfully detained by the Station House Officer at the instance of respondent No.2 therein.
Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:9496 4.

Perusal of the documents placed before this Court in particular I.A.No. 46618 of 2024 along with the documents enclosed therein as also the order impugned in this bail application would show that in Para-10 of I.A. No.46618 of 2024, the grievance raised is of dismissing the bail application dated 15.02.2024 by the learned Magistrate whereas the order Annexure A-1 against which this bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is filed is dated 22.02.2024.
By the order dated 22.02.2024, the application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. has been dismissed.

The contents of the order would further show that on 15.02.2024 when applicant was produced before the learned Magistrate in transit remand, application under Section 437 of Cr.P.C.
was filed.

Considering the fact that application under Section 439 filed by applicant was disposed of only on 22.02.2024, the objection raised by learned counsel for complainant/objector that in I.A.
No. 46618/24 filed on 16.02.2024 the prayer for bail is sought for, hence, the application is not maintainable, in the opinion of this Court is not sustainable and therefore, the objection raised by the learned counsel for complainant/objector is repelled.

5. Case of the prosecution in brief is that complainant has lodged a written complaint on 22.01.2024 in the concerned police station against applicant and one Kavish Gupta alleging that applicant after due deliberation and taking complainant in confidence had Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:9496 issued work order on 30.12.2020 for construction of S.T.P.
After allotment of work, complainant has started the work immediately thereafter because, it has to be completed at the earliest.

Company of the complainant has completed about 30% of the work allotted to her of which entire amount is expended by company of complainant and against which complainant has also raised bill of Rs.2,69,66,995/- against which complainant was paid only Rs.1,50,78,579/- and rest of the amount was not paid stating that it will be paid at later point of time.

The work allotted to the complainant by applicant company i.e. M/s. K.K. Spun Pvt. Ltd. was awarded to the said company by Municipal Corporation, Satna, which was already terminated prior to awarding of the work to complainant company and likewise complainant was not paid the entire bills of the work done by her company Himanshu Gupta vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85602880/
2 allotted by the company of applicant and thereby the complainant was cheated.

sentences.text: It is further allegation that applicant has withdrawn amount from the employer by raising forged and fabricated bills in the name of firm/company of the complainant.
Based on the report, aforementioned crime was registered on the same day i.e. on 22.01.2024 and applicant was arrested on 14.02.2024.
6. Learned Senior counsel appearing on behalf of applicant would submit that report lodged against applicant is false and lodged with ulterior motive.

He contended that company of the applicant M/s.
K.K. Spun Pvt. Ltd. sublet the awarded work to M/s. S.R. Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:9496 Construction of which complainant is proprietor and also to Ansh Infra.
Same complaint was made by both the proprietorship firm against applicant before Superintendent of Police in which applicant was called for enquiry on 12.07.2023.
During pendency of that enquiry M/s. Ansh Infra lodged a report on 20.07.2023 in the concerned police station which was registered as Crime No.218 of 2023.
Applicant filed an application for grant of anticipatory bail, which was dismissed by learned Sessions Court as also by the High Court.

Against the rejection of an application for grant of anticipatory bail, applicant filed Special Leave to Appeal (Criminal) No.371 of 2024, which came up for hearing on 10.01.2024 and Hon'ble Supreme Court has passed an interim protective order in favour of applicant observing that "In the meantime, the petitioner shall not be arrested subject to condition that he shall cooperate with the investigation".

entities.text: Special Leave to Appeal (Criminal) No.371 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: It is only after passing of an order dated 10.01.2024, complainant has filed a written complaint to the concerned police station on 22.01.2024 and on the same day, the FIR was registered which is only with an intent to frustrate the order of Hon'ble Apex Court to see that some how applicant be arrested.
Complainant herein has raised the grievance before the Superintendent of Police (Crime), District Raipur as early on 12.07.2023.

The complainant filed written report to concerned Police Station to overcome with the order of interim protection in favour of applicant by Hon'ble Supreme Court on 22.01.2024 in which the complainant also Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:9496 succeed as applicant was arrested without following the direction issued by the Ho'ble Supreme Court in case of Arnesh Kumar (supra).
Applicant was arrested from Delhi.
7. It is next contended by learned Senior Counsel for applicant that no offence as alleged under Section 420 of I.P.C. would be made out against applicant.
There was a contract between the firm/company of applicant with the firm of complainant.
She completed part of the work out of which part payment was also paid and therefore, the dispute between them is purely of civil nature.

Only to give colour to the civil dispute of criminal, allegation is made that suppressing the material fact of termination of contract, work allotted to applicant company/firm was sublet to complainant's firm, which was per-se wrong and baseless.

He contended that though the office of Municipal Corporation, Satna vide order dated 21.04.2020 has issued letter of termination of contract under Clause-27 of agreement of sewerage project, during first phase of Covid-19 pandemic and also the lock-down period.

Against termination of contract, applicant availed the remedy available under the contract, of dispute resolution before Superintending Engineer and the Superintending Engineer,
Urban Administration Development Department had taken decision on the application/claim of applicant firm/company and decided that Municipal Corporation to consider the suspension of the decision of termination of Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:9496 contract and allied activity for the next six months from the date of receiving of order and further directed the director/firm of applicant to submit monthly work programme for next six months to be mutually agreed upon by Himanshu Gupta vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85602880/

sentences.text: 3 Municipal Corporation, Satna PDMC and contractor.
On successfully achiveing the six months time line progress Municipal Corporation may review the decision of termination of contract accordingly.

The decision was communicated on 04.07.2020 and it is only thereafter, the complainant was allotted the work for construction of STP in the month of December, 2020 and therefore, on the date of allotting the work by way of subletting the order of termination of contract was not in force as it was suspended.
With respect to allegation of forged bills raised by applicant, it is submitted that it can be proved by the documentary evidence as the bills are in the possession of Municipal Corporation.
Applicant is in jail since 14.02.2024, no custodial interrogation is required, hence, he may be enlarged on regular bail.

8. It is also submitted by learned Senior counsel that considering the similar nature of allegation levelled in Crime No.218/2023, registered in Police Station Vidhansabha, Raipur Hon'ble Supreme Court has granted interim protection of not to arrest applicant in Special Leave to Appeal against the order of rejection of application for grant of anticipatory bail.

In support of his contention, he places reliance upon the decision of Hon'ble Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:9496 Supreme Court in case of V.P. Shrivastava Vs. Indian Explosives Limited & Ors. reported in (2010) 10 SCC 361, in case of Dilip Kaur & Ors. Vs. Jagnar Singh & Anr. reported in (2009) 14 SCC 696.
9.

sentences.text:
Learned State counsel opposes the submission of learned counsel for applicant and would submit that written report is filed by complainant alleging that complainant was awarded the work, on subletting by applicant firm/company, of which complainant has also executed part of the work,
however, she was not made aware about the termination of the contract awarded to M/s. K.K.Spun Pvt. Ltd. of which applicant is one of the director.
He submits that there is no error in rejecting the application for grant of bail.

Upon asking whether any notice was issued to applicant after receipt of complaint and registration of FIR before his arrest, he submits that though in the case diary one notice in the name of applicant is available, however, it is not signed and dated.
He further submits that it appears that notice was not issued to applicant prior to his arrest.
Upon asking he further submits that till date police has not seized any bills from the office of Municipal Corporation, Satna.

10. Mr. Siddharth Dubey, learned counsel for objector/complainant raises an objection with regard to grant of bail and would submit that complainant was induced by applicant for doing the work under contract agreement executed between applicant's Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:9496 firm/company and complainant's firm, complainant firm has completed the part of work.

The termination of contract was finalized in the month of April, 2020, however, the work was allotted/awarded in favour of complainant/firm in the month of December and therefore,
prima-facie complainant was cheated.
11. I have heard learned counsel for parties and perused the documents placed before this Court and the case diary.

12. Perusal of the documents placed along with bail application in particular Annexure A-6 would show that one FIR was lodged by Ajay Nair, Proprietor of M/s. Ansh Infrastructure and Developers on 20.07.2023 bearing Crime No.218 of 2023 for alleged commission of offence under Section 420,
34 of I.P.C..

Perusal of the contents of FIR would show that similar nature of allegation of Himanshu Gupta vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85602880/
4 withdrawal of amount through forged bills was levelled and further subletting the work on 30.12.2020 whereas contract was terminated on 21.04.2020 by the Municipal Corporation, Satna.
Anticipatory bail application was filed, which came to be dismissed by District and Sessions Court as also by the High Court, against which, Special Leave to Appeal (Criminal) No. 371 of 2024 was filed,
which came up for hearing on 10.01.2024 and the Hon'ble Supreme Court had passed the following orders :-
"The complainant is added as respondent No.2 in the present Special leave Petitions.

In the meantime, the petitioner shall not be arrested subject to condition that he shall co-operate with the investigation."
13.
Hon'ble Supreme Court by the above order has granted interim protection to petitioner from arrest subject to condition that he will co-operate with investigation.

From the documents placed in record along with bail application i.e. copy of the e-mails, filed along with supplementary affidavit would show that the firm of the complainant and Ansh Infrastructure are aware of the activities and steps taken because in the e-mail of complainant subject ws of Ansh Infra - KAtni. Bill-01 is mentioned in the FIR lodged by complainant would show that complainant completed work awarded to her firm on 30.12.2020 to the extent of 30% and out of Rs.2,69,66,995/-,
Rs.1,50,78,579/- was paid but remaining amount was not paid.

14. From the contents of FIR it is appearing that report was lodged on account of non-payment of part of the amount due to complainant towards the work, she executed pursuant to the contract agreement executed between the parties.

The documents enclosed by applicant as Annexure SA-4,
which is proceeding of the office of the Urban Administration Development Department in arbitration case would show that contract awarded to applicant/company of Sewerage Project Municipal Corporation Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:9496 Satna was terminated on 21.04.2020 against which applicant has submitted an application on 27.06.2020 under Clause 12 of the General Conditions of Contract for dispute resolution in which the Superintending Engineer, Urban Administration Development Department concluded and decided that Municipal Corporation, Satna to consider the suspension of decision of termination of contract and allied activity for the next six months from the date of receiving of order.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Decision of Superintending Engineer was enclosed along with covering letter dated 04.07.2020.

15. Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Arnesh Kumar (supra) has considered the provisions under Section 41-A of the Cr.P.C. and observed that notice of appearance in terms of Section 41-A of Cr.P.C. be served on the accused within two weeks from the date of institution of the case, which may be extended by the Superintendent of Police of the District for the reasons to be recorded in writing.

The offence complained in case of Arnesh Kumar (supra) was of under Section 498 A of Himanshu Gupta vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85602880/
5

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I.P.C., however, Hon'ble Supreme Court further clarified that directions aforesaid shall not only apply to the cases under Section 498-A of the I.P.C. or Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, but also to such cases where offence is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may be less than seven years or which may extend to seven years.

16. For the forgoing discussions and considering the fact that Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:9496 applicant is in custody since 14.02.2024, it appears that no custodial interrogation is required, this Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case to enlarge the applicant on regular bail.
17. Accordingly, the bail application filed under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on regular bail upon his furnishing a bail bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- with one local surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the Court below on the conditions that:-
a). Applicant shall appear before the trial Court regularly on each and every date,
unless exempted from appearance.
(b).
Applicant shall not, in any manner, tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
c). If the applicant is found involved in similar offence in the future, it will be open for the State to apply for cancellation of Bail.
Certified copy as per rules.
